chunks: My father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with them) narrated, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The tradition regarding hair removal (al-nurah) is every fifteen days. If twenty-one days pass (without doing so), one should borrow money for God's sake and perform hair removal. If forty days pass and one has not performed hair removal, he is neither a believer nor a Muslim, and there is no honor for him.

key_terms.السُّنَّة: The prophetic tradition or recommended practice
key_terms.النَّوْرَة: Hair removal (specifically from the armpits and pubic area)
key_terms.يَتَنَوَّرْ: To perform hair removal (verb form from Nurah)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended frequency for hair removal in Shia Islam and what are the consequences of delaying it?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith to establish a specific fiqh benchmark for *al-nurah* (general body hair removal), distinguishing between the recommended interval of fifteen days and the maximum tolerance of twenty-one days before one must prioritize the act even at a cost. The severe consequence of exceeding forty days—loss of *karāmah* (dignity/honor) and status as a believer—highlights the Shia emphasis on *fitrah* (natural disposition) and physical purity as integral components of spiritual identity. This ruling reflects the broader scholarly tradition that views personal hygiene not merely as cleanliness, but as a marker of religious observance and social dignity.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 15-7 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father and Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid - may God be pleased with them - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, on the authority of some friends that Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) said, “

Applying depilatory7 once every fifteen days is a tradition. You should borrow money for doing so, if you cannot apply depilatory for twenty-one days. You are neither a Muslim nor a believer, if you do not apply depilatory for more than forty days. You are not honorable either.”
